name: Undecidability of the word problem: logic and computability enter group theory
summary: After Dehn posed decision problems for presented groups and Church proposed a logical route, Post, Markov, Boone and Novikov proved word problems insoluble and Higman's embedding theorem tied recursive presentation to finite presentation.

name: Weyl's Riemann surface and abstract manifold concept
summary: Weyl gave a rigorous definition of Riemann surface as a topological manifold with charts.

name: Hausdorff dimension: measure meets dimension theory
summary: Hausdorff allowed non-integer dimensions defined metrically, Besicovitch developed the theory, and Mandelbrot's fractal definition set it against topological dimension.

name: Model theory beginnings
summary: Loewenheim and Skolem showed that first-order theories with infinite models have countable ones, opening semantic study of formal theories.

name: Noether's theorem: symmetries and conservation laws
summary: Hilbert's variational derivation of gravitation led to identities that Noether tied to symmetries, giving her 1918 theorem.

name: Affine connections (Levi-Civita, Weyl)
summary: Levi-Civita introduced parallel transport, Weyl generalised to gauge geometry, and Cartan developed connections and moving frames.

name: Hardy-Littlewood circle method
summary: Contour integration of generating functions and exponential sums are used to count representations of integers (partitions, sums of primes), the method behind later Fourier-analytic density arguments.

name: Fisher statistical inference
summary: Fisher unified chi-squared, small-sample t and variance analysis into a framework tested on Rothamsted crop data.

name: Banach spaces
summary: Banach defined complete normed spaces and proved the key theorems on operators, forming the Lwow school.
